% ----------------------- BIDI ------------------------------------
% XeTeX's OpenType shaper already reverses the LETTERS inside each
% Arabic-script word, but places the WORDS of a run left-to-right.  The
% TeXXeT primitives \beginR/\endR reverse box order inside a segment.
% Omitting them reproduces the classic bug: correct letters, LTR
% word order.  Adding them twice (e.g. via a bidi package on top)
% double-reverses.  Do not change this without re-running `verify`.
% The state is switched on for every language: the primitives are only
% emitted (by texgen) for a right-to-left target.
\TeXXeTstate=1

% Hyphenation follows the document's own `lang:` front matter, mapped to
% a TeX language name by texgen.hyphenation_for().  Applying one
% language's patterns to another is worse than applying none (English
% rules break Italian as "br-usco"; Italian rules break English just as
% badly), so the language is activated ONLY if the running format really
% carries it — otherwise TeX keeps its default, language 0, US English.
% Italian is the one set of patterns exlex ships and installs itself,
% since many TeX Live installs lack it; see envsetup.py.
\expandafter\ifx\csname l@%%HYPHENLANG%%\endcsname\relax\else
  \language=\csname l@%%HYPHENLANG%%\endcsname
  \lefthyphenmin=%%HYPHENLMIN%% \righthyphenmin=%%HYPHENRMIN%%
\fi

% ----------------------- GLYPH FALLBACK --------------------------
% TeX Gyre Pagella and Heros have æ ð θ ŋ ə and none of the rest of the IPA
% -- ʊ ɪ ɑ ʃ ʒ ɛ ɔ ʌ, the stress mark, the length mark -- and XeTeX, unlike
% the LuaLaTeX of the reading editions (lib/frank-preamble.tex hands
% luaotfload DejaVu Serif), has no glyph fallback: each one was a hole in
% the PDF and a "Missing character" line in the log, while the build still
% reported every target string verified.  A pronunciation reaches the body
% text of any document -- a flashcard copied from an English book carries
% its IPA line -- so the fallback is made here, by hand: every character of
% the blocks below that the body face LACKS and DejaVu Serif HAS gets an
% inter-character class of its own, and XeTeX sets a run of them in DejaVu
% (Serif, or Sans in sans text, Sans Mono in typewriter text) scaled to the
% body face's x-height, at the size, weight and shape around it.  A
% character the body face has is never touched, so a document without one
% of those characters sets exactly as before.  A combining mark the body
% face has is left out of the class machinery ("ignored"), so it stays in
% the face of the letter it sits on.  A machine without DejaVu Serif gets
% no fallback, and the holes, as before.
\newcount\exlexfbchar
% \exlexfbblock{first}{last}{1 for a block of combining marks}
\def\exlexfbblock#1#2#3{%
  \exlexfbchar=#1\relax
  \loop
    \ifnum\XeTeXcharclass\exlexfbchar=0
      \iffontchar\exlexfbbody\exlexfbchar
        \ifnum#3=1 \global\XeTeXcharclass\exlexfbchar=\exlexfbignored\fi
      \else\iffontchar\exlexfbface\exlexfbchar
        \global\XeTeXcharclass\exlexfbchar=\exlexfbclass
      \fi\fi
    \fi
  \ifnum\exlexfbchar<#2 \advance\exlexfbchar 1 \repeat}
% Into the fallback before the first character of a run, out after its
% last: a group, so the face around it (NFSS's family, series, shape, size)
% comes back whole.  The flag keeps the two paired -- nothing but those
% characters can come between them, since anything else ends the run.
\def\exlexfbon{%
  \ifx\exlexfbin\relax\else
    \begingroup\let\exlexfbin\relax
    \edef\exlexfbfam{\csname f@family\endcsname}%
    \edef\exlexfbsf{\sfdefault}\edef\exlexfbtt{\ttdefault}%
    \ifx\exlexfbfam\exlexfbsf\exlexfbsans
    \else\ifx\exlexfbfam\exlexfbtt\exlexfbmono
    \else\exlexfbserif\fi\fi
  \fi}
\def\exlexfboff{\ifx\exlexfbin\relax\expandafter\endgroup\fi}
\IfFontExistsTF{DejaVu Serif}{%
  \newfontfamily\exlexfbserif{DejaVu Serif}[Scale=MatchLowercase]%
  \IfFontExistsTF{DejaVu Sans}%
    {\newfontfamily\exlexfbsans{DejaVu Sans}[Scale=MatchLowercase]}%
    {\let\exlexfbsans\exlexfbserif}%
  \IfFontExistsTF{DejaVu Sans Mono}%
    {\newfontfamily\exlexfbmono{DejaVu Sans Mono}[Scale=MatchLowercase]}%
    {\let\exlexfbmono\exlexfbsans}%
  \newXeTeXintercharclass\exlexfbclass
  \chardef\exlexfbignored=\numexpr\csname e@alloc@intercharclass@top\endcsname+1\relax
  {\normalfont\expandafter\global\expandafter\let\expandafter\exlexfbbody\the\font
   \exlexfbserif\expandafter\global\expandafter\let\expandafter\exlexfbface\the\font}%
  \exlexfbblock{"0180}{"024F}0% Latin Extended-B (the click letters among them)
  \exlexfbblock{"0250}{"02AF}0% IPA Extensions
  \exlexfbblock{"02B0}{"02FF}0% Spacing Modifier Letters (stress, length, tone)
  \exlexfbblock{"0300}{"036F}1% Combining Diacritical Marks
  \exlexfbblock{"0370}{"03FF}0% Greek (beta, chi)
  \exlexfbblock{"1D00}{"1DBF}0% Phonetic Extensions and their Supplement
  \exlexfbblock{"1DC0}{"1DFF}1% Combining Diacritical Marks Supplement
  \exlexfbblock{"1E00}{"1EFF}0% Latin Extended Additional
  \exlexfbblock{"2070}{"209F}0% Superscripts and Subscripts
  \exlexfbblock{"2190}{"21FF}0% Arrows (the tone arrows)
  \exlexfbblock{"A700}{"A7FF}0% Modifier Tone Letters, Latin Extended-D
  % into the class from every other one, the boundary included, and out
  \exlexfbchar=0
  \loop
    \ifnum\exlexfbchar=\exlexfbclass\else
      \XeTeXinterchartoks\exlexfbchar\exlexfbclass={\exlexfbon}%
      \XeTeXinterchartoks\exlexfbclass\exlexfbchar={\exlexfboff}%
    \fi
  \ifnum\exlexfbchar<\csname e@alloc@intercharclass@top\endcsname
    \advance\exlexfbchar 1 \repeat
  \XeTeXinterchartokenstate=1
}{}

% ----------------------- LEMMA HEADER ----------------------------
% \voce{headword}{reading}{transliteration}{etymology}: the reading line
% (the kana of a Japanese lemma) is printed above the transliteration
% and only when given -- every other language passes it empty.
%
% The headword is measured before it is set, and a headword wider than
% its column is scaled down by exactly as much as it takes to fit.  Some
% languages prescribe long ones: German's noun form is "die
% Geschwindigkeitsbegrenzung, -en" (docs/lang/de.md) and Turkish
% agglutinates a lemma with no space anywhere in it -- three times this
% column at %%VOCESIZE%%pt, and unscaled the word ran across the
% transliteration and off the paper.  Wrapping instead is not open to us:
% the long ones are single words, so the break would have to fall inside
% the word, and a hyphen inside a German compound is the one thing that
% language's conventions forbid.  One line per lemma is also what lets
% the eye run down the sheet.  A headword that already fits is set from
% the very box that measured it, so short lemmas are untouched.
\newsavebox{\voceheadbox}
\newcommand{\voce}[4]{%
  \needspace{9\baselineskip}%
  \par\vspace{1.4ex}%
  {\color{rulec}\hrule height 1.1pt}%
  \vspace{0.5ex}%
  \noindent\parbox[b]{0.60\linewidth}{\raggedright
      \sbox{\voceheadbox}{\fontsize{%%VOCESIZE%%}{%%VOCELEAD%%}\selectfont\pe{#1}}%
      \ifdim\wd\voceheadbox>\linewidth
        \resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{\usebox{\voceheadbox}}%
      \else\usebox{\voceheadbox}\fi}%
  \hfill
  \parbox[b]{0.38\linewidth}{\raggedleft
      \if\relax\detokenize{#2}\relax\else%%VOCEFIT%%{\small\tlfont #2}\\[0.2ex]\fi
      %%VOCEFIT%%{\large\itshape\color{accent}\trfont #3}\\[0.2ex]
      %%VOCEFIT%%{\footnotesize\color{graytx}#4}}%
  \par\vspace{0.6ex}%
  {\color{rulec}\hrule height 0.5pt}%
  \par\vspace{1.0ex}}
